q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT serves1.bar, serves2.bar FROM serves AS serves1 RIGHT OUTER JOIN serves AS serves2 ON serves1.beer = serves2.beer AND serves1.bar <> serves2.bar

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 checks for bars that serve a beer which no other bar serves, while Q2 checks for bars that serve a beer which at least one other bar does not serve.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two bars, 'Bar A' and 'Bar B', and a beer 'Beer X' that 'Bar A' serves but 'Bar B' does not serve. 'Bar B' should serve another beer 'Beer Y' that 'Bar A' does not serve.
